{{Quote|It was perhaps one of the darkest moments of the war.|Grand Master Satele Shan|<ref name="JoMGD" />}}
The '''Blockade of the Hydian Way''' was an offensive action against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian warrior clans]] in the final decade of the [[Great Galactic War]]. The [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] was orchestrated by the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire's]] [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Ministry of Intelligence]], which had spent years investing in the resurrection of the then-disbanded Mandalorian clans. The Empire's efforts culminated with the rise of [[Mandalore the Lesser]], who was little more than a puppet for the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] government. Disaffected Mandalorians from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] rallied to the man regardless and acquiesced to Imperial demands for support in their decades-long war against the Republic. After a series of skirmishes between Mandalorians and Jedi, the warriors launched their primary operation in [[3661 BBY]]. That year, [[Mandalorian cruiser]]s seized control of the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], a vital trade and supply route used by the Republic to move goods and resources from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] to civilian population centers in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], as well as [[Republic Military/Legends|military]] materiel bound for battlefronts across the galaxy.

The blockade was incredibly successful and choked commerce in the Republic's private [[Sector/Legends|sector]] and prevented military wares from reaching battlefields along the Hydian Way. The Core Worlds were thrown into an economic crisis, and the Republic's [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] was deadlocked on a proper course of action. After much deliberation, the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|High Council]] of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] consented to give aid by dispatching [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]] of [[Jedi ace|Jedi pilots]] to [[Battle near Devaron|confront]] the Mandalorian warships. Despite their strategies and [[The Force/Legends|Force]] talents, the Jedi fighter squadrons were handily defeated in an operation that was widely seen as a resounding failure. News of the Jedi defeat caused widespread panic and [[Coruscant riots (3661 BBY)|rioting]] on the Republic's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where impoverished peoples in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|lower levels]] of the planet-spanning [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] were beginning to suffer from starvation as a result of the supply crisis.

The blockade continued for a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] until [[3660 BBY]], when the [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Hylo Visz]] recognized it as an opportunity for profit. Together with a [[Hylo Visz's smuggling contingent|band]] of her fellow smugglers and financial backing from the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], Visz arranged for a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] to be loaded with much-needed goods from the Outer Rim Territories. The smugglers piloted the cargo haulers towards the blockade, and while the Mandalorians were distracted by the apparently defenseless shipping vessels, Visz and her allies [[Battle on the Hydian Way|attacked]] with a fleet of smuggling vessels. Their ambush was soon joined by Republic reinforcements that helped to overwhelm the Mandalorian [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]]. The blockade was ultimately broken in the engagement, and Hylo Visz was able to bring her goods to Coruscant, where she was greeted as a hero. Despite the victory, the Republic was irreparably inundated following the blockade and continued to suffer heavy losses throughout the war as a result.

==Prelude==
===The Sith in reflection===
{{Quote|When the Emperor planned the Republic's destruction, he did not foresee the need for alliances. The Sith would sweep through the galaxy, systematically exterminating their age-old Jedi enemies and dismantling the proud Republic. But the Emperor's vision was cynical. He did not count on the brave sacrifices the Republic's heroes were willing to make.|Gnost-Dural|<ref name="Timeline5">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui|int=Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui}}</ref>}}
After conducting an overwhelmingly successful campaign for dominance over the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] early in the [[Great Galactic War]],<ref name="Timeline6">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 6: Onslaught of the Sith Empire}}</ref> the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] failed in their [[Battle of Bothawui (Second; Great Galactic War)|attempt]] to take the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]]<ref name="Timeline5" /> in [[3671 BBY]].<ref name="BothawuiDate">According to ''[[Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui]]'', this conflict occurs eighteen years before the [[Treaty of Coruscant]]. The Treaty was proposed and ratified in [[3653 BBY]], as seen in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and the novel ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''.</ref> The massacre of nearly 50,000 [[Imperial Army (Sith Empire)|Imperial Army]] units at Bothawui<ref name="Timeline5" /> and the defeat of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] in the [[Battle of Alderaan]]<ref name="JoMGD" /> in [[3667 BBY]]<ref name="Date">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']] indicates that the Battle of Alderaan occurs four years after the [[Battle of Bothawui (Second; Great Galactic War)|Battle of Bothawui]]. According to ''[[Timeline 5: The Battle of Bothawui]]'' the Battle of Bothawui occurs eighteen years before the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], which, as seen in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]'', is proposed and ratified in [[3653 BBY]]. Thusly, the Battle of Bothawui takes place in [[3671 BBY]], and the Battle of Alderaan occurs four years later, in [[3667 BBY]].</ref> forced the Imperials to re-evaluate their warpath and re-examine the strategies that had served them well up until that point.<ref name="Timeline4">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 4: The Empire Changes Strategy|int=Timeline 4: The Empire Changes Strategy}}</ref> The [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] himself was humbled by the tenacity of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] defenders, as he had hoped that after the Empire's return to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], his victory in the Great War would be achieved in short order.<ref name="Timeline5" /> Much to his chagrin, the war was well into its third decade with no immediate resolution in sight,<ref name="JoMGD" /> even in light of consecutive Imperial victories prior to the Battles of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] and Bothawui.<ref name="Timeline5" />

Until this point in the war, the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] had widely ignored the need for allies, and instead blazed a path of conquest across the galaxy with Sith and Imperial forces alone.<ref name="Timeline5" /> This independence was the primary point of reform that Imperial tacticians focused on when they began to rework their strategies<ref name="Timeline4" /> in 3667 BBY.<ref name="Timeline4date">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 4: The Empire Changes Strategy|int=Timeline 4: The Empire Changes Strategy}} is placed fourteen years prior to the ratification of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], which is signed and implemented in [[3653 BBY]], as seen in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref> In that year, representatives of the [[Imperial Diplomatic Service]] began to actively solicit [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]], criminal syndicates, [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] for assistance in their war. Along with the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], these groups had been debating whether to support the Republic or the Empire since the start of the war, and active courting by Imperial [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]] did little to alter their indecisive demeanor.<ref name="Timeline4" />

===The Mandalorians enter the war===
{{Quote|The whispers of Imperial Agents became cheers in the arena. The ancient title of ultimate warrior-king was thrust upon the young gladiator. His infamy grew, and when he called, the Mandalorians rallied to their new master.|Gnost-Dural, on the rise of the new Mandalore|<ref name="Timeline4" />}}
[[File:Mandalor_GSW_rally.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Mandalorians reunite under their new Mandalore.]]
During this time, the Imperial Diplomatic Service also tried to convince individual [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] of the disbanded [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior tradition to serve the Sith. Although the Mandalorians of the era were disparate and divided,<ref name="Timeline4" /> many of their peoples still maintained a long-standing resentment of the Galactic Republic and [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] in light of their brutal treatment at the end of the [[Mandalorian Wars]] [[3960 BBY|three centuries prior]]&mdash;a characteristic that made them ideal tools of the Sith.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Several Mandalorians,<ref name="Timeline4" /> including the bounty hunter [[Mandalore the Avenger|Shae Vizla]],<ref name="JoMGD" /> signed on to serve alongside regular Imperial forces, but the vast majority of the warriors rejected the Sith offer, opting instead to remain independent nomads.<ref name="Timeline4" /> Although Vizla and her compatriots served faithfully, the Imperials still sought to stack the deck in their favor by gaining the allegiance of all Mandalore's warriors.<ref name="JoMGD" />

The duty of bringing the resistant Mandalorians into the Sith fold eventually fell to the Empire's [[Imperial Intelligence (Sith Empire)|Ministry of Intelligence]]&mdash;a highly effective and well-trained espionage agency staffed entirely by non-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Imperials. [[Imperial Agent]]s focused their efforts on one individual: a [[Mandalore the Lesser|young Mandalorian]] who had taken a career as a [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiator]] in the arenas of the Outer Rim world of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].<ref name="Timeline4" /> The operatives used their power and influence to rig the gladiator's bouts, either by buying off his opponents, drugging them,<ref name="JoMGD" /> or even by entering themselves in the bouts.<ref name="Timeline4" /> As the young man's reputation spread, they began to leak rumors around kennels and [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]] that the new champion was poised to become the next [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|Mandalore]]&mdash;the legendary title of the warrior-king that led the Mandalorian people. Despite there not having been a Mandalore for many decades, the agent's whispers spread quickly, becoming chants in the arena crowds. In doing so, the Imperials ensured that the young man owed his rise to them, and that he would therefore be little more than a puppet for Sith interests.<ref name="JoMGD" />

In [[3665 BBY]],<ref name="3665BBY">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']] indicates that the Mandalore takes the title and forms his army twelve years prior to the [[Treaty of Coruscant]]. As seen in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]'', the Treaty is ratified in [[3653 BBY]], meaning that these events would occur in [[3665 BBY]].</ref> shortly before he would have been forced to retire from arena combat, the gladiator resigned on his own accord. It was then that he formally accepted the title of Mandalore and summoned his people to Geonosis to reconstitute the Mandalorian armies.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Heeding their ancient traditions, Mandalorians from across the galaxy flocked to the Outer Rim and jumped at the opportunity to fight as one against their worthy long-time adversaries: the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the Republic.<ref name="Timeline4" /> [[3664 BBY|One year later]],<ref name="3664BBY">[[The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural (real-life book)|''The Journal of Master Gnost-Dural'']] indicates that the Mandalorian army departs Geonosis eleven years prior to the [[Treaty of Coruscant]]. As seen in ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]'', the Treaty is ratified in [[3653 BBY]], meaning that these events would occur in [[3664 BBY]].</ref> shortly before he would have been forced to retire from arena combat, the gladiator resigned on his own accord. It was then that the new Mandalorian army left Geonosis and initiated a series of engagements and skirmishes with the Jedi and [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] over the course of the following three years.<ref name="JoMGD" />

==The blockade==
===A crippled Republic===
{{Main|Battle near Devaron|Coruscant riots (3661 BBY)}}
{{Quote|The blockade choked the primary trade route for providing Republic military support to the Outer Rim and the main hyperlane for bringing raw goods from the Colonies to the Core Worlds. Long-standing hold-outs in the Outer Rim began folding to the Empire and critical supplies vanished from the Core Worlds almost overnight.|Gnost-Dural|audio=BlockadeChoked.flac|<ref name="Timeline2" />}}
After three years of minor battles between Jedi and Mandalorians, the warrior nomads initiated their primary operation. At the behest of the Imperials to whom he was beholden, the Mandalore gathered his people to form a small armada of [[Mandalorian cruiser|war cruisers]] and support [[Starship/Legends|ships]]<ref name="JoMGD" /> in [[3661 BBY]].<ref name="Startdate" /> The warrior-king took his new fleet to the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]]<ref name="JoMGD" />&mdash;a [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] that connected the far northern reaches of the galaxy in the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]] to the southern Outer Rim via the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The Republic relied heavily upon the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] as a passage for goods and resources produced in the Outer Rim Territories to support its bastion worlds in the Core, particularly its [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]];<ref name="Timeline2" /> furthermore, the Republic Military utilized the lane to move war materiel from the Core to battlefronts of the Great War in the deep Outer Rim. With his new fleet of war cruisers and [[Shock trooper/Legends|shock troops]], Mandalore initiated a blockade of the Hydian Way in the southern section of the route between the planet [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]]<ref name="JoMGD" /> in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]]<ref name="TEA" /> and the long-[[Minos Cluster Campaign|embattled]] worlds of the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]] in the southern Outer Rim.<ref name="JoMGD" />

[[File:Coruscant_riot.jpg|thumb|left|280px|One of the many riots that broke out on Coruscant in response to the supply crisis]]
The blockade came as a shock to Republic officials, who had been uncertain of the exact size and strength of the Mandalorian forces. Although the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] would normally have been able to quickly deal with the relatively small blockade, the fleet was still reeling after a [[Battle of Hoth (Great Galactic War)|devastating engagement]] with the [[Imperial Navy (Sith Empire)|Imperial Navy]] above the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] four years prior. With its commercial and military lifeline in a Mandalorian stranglehold, the Galactic Republic began to falter after years of success in the war.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Assets in the Outer Rim which had successfully stood up against Imperial subjugation for years began to fold under the dual pressures of Sith attacks and supply deficits.<ref name="Timeline2" /> Republic fighters in the Minos Cluster lost considerable ground,<ref name="JoMGD" /> and the Empire's [[Rim Campaign]] was able to make considerable headway on the planet [[Ord Radama/Legends|Ord Radama]], as significant reinforcements were prevented from reaching the local forces [[Battle of Ord Radama|battling]] Sith invaders.<ref name="BookOfSith" /> Additionally, critical supplies produced in the Outer Rim and Colonies were prevented from reaching the Core, drying up shipping [[Spaceport/Legends|ports]] and creating a severe food shortage crisis on worlds such as Coruscant.<ref name="Timeline2" />

The few supplies that were available within the Core disappeared rapidly,<ref name="Timeline2" /> worsening the considerable [[Galactic economy|economic]] depression that the Republic had been suffering through since the start of the war.<ref name="Republic">{{Holonet|allegiances|galactic-republic|The Galactic Republic}}</ref> As starvation began to sweep the planet's [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|lower levels]], the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] appealed to the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|High Council]] of the Jedi Order to take action against the Mandalorians. The Jedi were hesitant to agree, as they were wary of pulling their [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]] away from conflicts with the Sith.<ref name="Timeline3" /> Furthermore, their history of conflict with the Mandalorians led them to believe that the warrior nomads were only blockading the Hydian Way in order to goad the Jedi into a fight; the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Councilors]] had moral reservations about rewarding the Mandalorians with a battle they were so eager to wage, but felt they had a duty to try to alleviate the crippling famine that was striking Coruscant's poor.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Deciding that they could ignore neither the economic crisis,<ref name="Timeline3" /> the suffering of civilians, nor the boon that the blockade was giving the Imperial war effort, the Jedi agreed to launch an attack.<ref name="JoMGD" />

Under the leadership of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]], including the [[Kel Dor/Legends|Kel Dor]] [[Jedi historian]] [[Gnost-Dural]], a group of [[Jedi ace|Jedi pilots]] moved against the blockade in [[Aurek-class tactical strikefighter|''Aurek''-class tactical strikefighters]]. [[Battle near Devaron|The battle]] was short but fierce, and ultimately proved to be an embarrassing defeat for the Jedi Order. While the few survivors limped back to regroup at Devaron, the blockade continued unimpeded. When news of the Jedi defeat reached Coruscant, starving residents of the lower city began to stage [[Coruscant riots (3661 BBY)|mass riots]] in demand of food and economic support. The situation continued for weeks on end, with famine growing more severe and the rioters becoming increasingly violent and desperate.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Seeing their Republic starved and torn apart from within, many senators<ref name="Timeline2" />&mdash;even the most ardent war hawks<ref name="JoMGD" />&mdash;began to suggest that surrendering to the Sith may be the only viable recourse.<ref name="Timeline2" /> At some time during the blockade, a Mandalorian ship known as the [[Beskad (starship)|''Beskad'']] vanished and was thought to have been lost in a [[Black hole/Legends|black hole]]; however, it was discovered decades later that the ship had actually crashed elsewhere.<ref name="ROTHC" />

===Smugglers take the lead===
{{Main|Battle on the Hydian Way}}
{{Quote|Distracted by suspicious freighters, the Mandalorians never knew what hit them. A motley fleet of small starships dropped out of hyperspace and opened fire. A massive space battle ensued. The smugglers' light freighters ran rings around the Mandalorian cruisers&mdash;even so, Hylo Visz and her band were outmatched. Fortunately, Republic Strategic Information Systems was tipped off and starfighters were scrambled from nearby systems. With their assistance, the Mandalorians were quickly overcome.|Gnost-Dural|<ref name="Timeline2" />}}
[[File:Mandalorian_Blockade_is_broken.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Visz's band of smugglers assault the blockade.]]
Into this climate stepped [[Hylo Visz]], a [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] and rising underworld star who was looking to profit from the galactic crisis. Recognizing that the Republic would pay any price for much-needed goods, Visz gathered together a band of criminals and miscreants<ref name="Timeline2" />&mdash;including the adventurous young [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Zale Barrows]],<ref name="Zale">{{TORcite|type=codex|Captain Zale Barrows}}</ref> Visz's [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] partner [[Gault Rennow|Tyresius Lokai]], and his friend [[Quan]]<ref name="Gault">{{TORcite|type=class|Bounty Hunter|Conversation with [[Gault Rennow]]|ship}}</ref>&mdash;on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], where they agreed to form a small fleet and launch an operation to run and ultimately break the Mandalorian blockade of the Hydian Way.<ref name="JoMGD" /> [[Hylo Visz's smuggling contingent|Hylo's band]] of smugglers recruited [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and mercenaries to aid them and,<ref name="Timeline2" /> with financial backing from the criminal Hutt Cartel,<ref name="Gault" /> began to assemble a fleet of massive [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] loaded with cargo from across the Outer Rim Territories. This convoy, destined for Coruscant to relieve the starving residents, was piloted directly toward the Mandalorian blockade. The unarmed freighters halted within a single [[Parsec/Legends|parsec]] of the picketed cruisers&mdash;a position and action that puzzled the Mandalorians.<ref name="Timeline2" /> The warrior's cruisers hailed the vessels to demand that they turn back, but after receiving no response they moved to intercept the freighters.<ref name="JoMGD" />

It was at this moment that Visz and her allies sprang their trap; as the Mandalorians were distracted by the curious freighters, hundreds of small vessels and [[Transport/Legends|transports]] dropped out of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] and launched a [[Battle on the Hydian Way|surprise assault]] on the blockade.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Visz's band was initially highly successful in their attack, as their small starships easily outmaneuvered the large Mandalorian cruisers. However, despite the element of surprise and the advantage of speed, the smugglers were still outgunned by the Mandalorians. This changed when the [[Republic Strategic Information Service|Republic's Strategic Information Service]] learned of the battle<ref name="Timeline2" /> and dispatched elements of both the Republic Navy and the Jedi Order's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] fleet to ensure the attack's success.<ref name="JoMGD" /> Among the ships dispatched was a [[Valor-class cruiser|''Valor''-class cruiser]] named the [[Fortitude (Valor-class)|''Fortitude'']], a ship that gained popular fame for its role in the fighting.<ref name="An Alliance" /> The combined forces of the smugglers, the Republic, and the Jedi eventually overcame those of the Mandalorians, forcing the surviving warrior nomads to flee the battle. With the cruiser fleet routed, the Hydian Way was released from the grip of the blockade.<ref name="JoMGD" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|A closer look, however, suggests the Sacking of Coruscant was not the crowning moment of the Empire's campaign, but rather a risky maneuver undertaken after all other efforts had failed. The Sith only considered turning to such measures after their efforts were undermined by an unlikely Republic ally&mdash;the criminal smuggling contingent that broke the Mandalorian blockade.|Gnost-Dural|<ref name="Timeline2" />}}
Shortly after the battle, Hylo Visz and her band of miscreants landed on Coruscant with the freighters and were greeted as heroes. The group sold their goods to the Republic at highly inflated prices, but few in the government cared; the blockade had been broken thanks to Visz, so their payment would double as a reward.<ref name="JoMGD" /> The Mirialan earned incredible wealth in the days that followed and a was even honored by the Galactic Senate with a medal ceremony. She chose not to attend the event, however, and fled Coruscant with her riches before anyone learned of her destination. With the blockade broken, the Republic was able to resume the war effort against the Sith Empire, albeit in a diminished capacity.<ref name="Timeline2" /> Naval forces finally succeeded in traversing the Hydian Way and reaching Ord Radama, where they reinforced the local defenders in their desperate stand against the Sith. The battle there quickly turned into a route, and the Republic was able to follow the fleeing Sith back to the cradles of their civilization: [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]], and [[Ashas Ree/Legends|Ashas Ree]].<ref name="BookOfSith" />

[[File:Hylo_arrives.jpg||thumb|left|280px|Hylo Visz is hailed as a hero of the Republic upon her arrival at Coruscant.]]
As had happened after Bothawui<ref name="Timeline5" /> and Alderaan, the Republic rallied in response to the surprising upset of a victory on the Hydian Way.<ref name="JoMGD" /> One veteran of the attack, smuggler captain Zale Barrows, decided that instead of fleeing Coruscant as Visz had, he would take up employment as a freelance naval commander for the Republic. Acting as [[Admiral/Legends|admiral]] of the privateer [[Free Spacers Fleet]], Barrows helped to defeat the [[Imperial Third Fleet|Sith Empire's Third Fleet]] at the [[Battle of Dantooine (Great Galactic War)|Battle of Dantooine]] and later [[Defeat of the Imperial Seventh Fleet|removed]] the [[Imperial Seventh Fleet|Seventh Fleet]] from Imperial service as well.<ref name="Zale" /> However, unlike previous feats of spirit and dedication, the success of the attack on the Hydian was measured against both the damage that the blockade caused, as well as the Republic's other staggering defeats in the war. It was widely conceded that the breaking of the blockade served only to prolong the Republic's survival&mdash;not to move it any closer to victory.<ref name="Timeline2" />

In the immediate aftermath of the blockade's end, the defeated Mandalorians scattered once more, with some pursuing solo careers while others remained alongside their new Mandalore.<ref name="Timeline3" /> Despite their failure on the Hydian Way, the Mandalorians and Sith maintained their alliance for decades after the war.<ref name="Timeline4" /> The Sith, however, had reached a breaking point with regards to their willingness to continue waging the Great Galactic War. In response to the blockade's failure, the Emperor and his [[Dark Council]] sought to bring a quick end to the conflict, ultimately leading to more desperate and risky Imperial tactics, such as a [[Alderaan peace conference|peace ruse]] on the planet Alderaan and the violent and devastating [[Sacking of Coruscant]].<ref name="Timeline1">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Blockade of the Hydian Way was created as part of the Great Galactic War, which makes up the background story for [[LucasArts]]' and [[BioWare]]'s [[2011]] massively multiplayer online [[Star Wars video games|video game]], ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''. The Blockade of the Hydian Way was first mentioned in the [[Timeline 2: The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken|second]] installment of the ''[[Galactic Timeline]]'', an [[in-universe]] account of the history of the galaxy prior to the Treaty of Coruscant. This intallment, titled ''The Mandalorian Blockade is Broken'' introduces the character of Hylo Visz and is the first source to bring the Mandalorian warriors into ''The Old Republic'' media.<ref name="Timeline2" /> The timelines are narrated by actor [[Lance Henriksen]] as Jedi Master Gnost-Dural, and are available on the [http://www.swtor.com/info/holonet Holonet] feature on the [http://www.swtor.com ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' official website].<ref name="Galactic Timeline">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref>

It was originally established that the Hydian Way was charted around [[3000 BBY]]; however, this was later changed to have taken place around [[3700 BBY/Legends|3700 BBY]] so that the route could be used in ''The Old Republic''.<ref name="DW">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_28.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 4 of 5)}}</ref>
